record.original_question: Let F_*(n) denote a partial billiard complexity obtained by coding only orbit families satisfying additional restrictions; for example, periodic complexity counts periodic-orbit codes. Find nontrivial explicit bounds on such partial billiard complexities for a general polygon.

evidence.quote: Imposing various restrictions on the billiard orbits, we obtain conditional or partial complexities F_*(n). For instance, the function f_P(n) in Problem 11 is the periodic complexity for the billiard on P.
Problem 14. Find nontrivial, explicit bounds on partial billiard complexities for the general polygon.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a polygon in the plane and consider the billiard flow on $P$: a point particle moves in straight lines inside $P$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) on the sides, with trajectories meeting a vertex left undefined. Code each billiard orbit by the sequence of sides it hits, so that a finite trajectory of combinatorial length $n$ corresponds to a word of length $n$ in the alphabet of sides of $P$. The (full) billiard complexity $F(n)$ is the number of distinct admissible words of length $n$ realized by some billiard orbit in $P$.

A partial billiard complexity $F_*(n)$ is obtained by counting only those length-$n$ codes that come from orbits satisfying a prescribed restriction. Important examples include:
- the periodic complexity $f_P(n)$, the number of distinct codes of length $n$ realized by periodic billiard orbits in $P$;
- complexities counting only codes of orbits that are uniformly distributed, only codes of saddle connections, or only codes avoiding a prescribed subset of sides; and other natural restrictions.

Problem. For a general (not necessarily rational) polygon $P$, find nontrivial, explicit upper and/or lower bounds, as functions of $n$, for partial billiard complexities $F_*(n)$. In particular, give explicit nontrivial bounds for the periodic complexity $f_P(n)$ valid for every polygon $P$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., 2023–2025 papers on the complexity of polygonal billiards) establishes cubic complexity bounds for rational and typical polygons and superlinear lower bounds on periodic complexity for certain irrational polygons, but no explicit nontrivial bounds for partial billiard complexities of a general polygon are known. The problem of finding such bounds is still listed as open in surveys on polygonal billiards.

status_evidence.title: On the complexity of polygonal billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Complexity of the billiard in a typical polygon grows cubically; saddle connections grow quadratically along subsequences.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on full complexity for typical polygons, but general-polygon bounds for partial complexities remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Survey Lecture on Billiards (Schwartz)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discusses outstanding problems including bounds on periodic and partial complexities.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of explicit bounds on partial billiard complexities for general polygons is highlighted as open.

status_evidence.title: Lower bounds on growth rates of periodic billiard trajectories
status_evidence.snippet: For irrational polygons, periodic-orbit count can grow faster than n log^k n on open sets of polygons.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial lower bounds for periodic complexity are known; uniform explicit bounds remain open.
